chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And those who believe and their offspring follow them in faith, We will unite with them their offspring."
He (AS) said: "The sons fall short of the deeds of the fathers, so Allah, the Mighty and High, unites the sons with the fathers so that their eyes may rest."
ai.seo_question: How does Allah unite children with parents in Paradise if the children's deeds are lesser?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that Allah joins children to their parents in Paradise not because of shared merit, but to comfort the parents' hearts, illustrating the distinction between individual accountability and familial mercy. This narration is pivotal in Shia theology for explaining how the righteous can attain higher ranks (Darajat) through the faith of their progeny, reinforcing the concept of divine grace (Fadl) alongside justice (Adl).
